m_dialogEntries.m_dialog: Greetings, Understudy. I am pleased that we may finally be formally introduced.
I am called Sparck. It is my honor to serve as your Science Officer for this mission. Hm. Do I detect the invigorating smell of Ion Dust?
Excellent. Come, I will show you what the Ion Dust is for. And along the way, I can show you around the Spiral Ark. Please, follow me.
This is the Ark's main machine room, which I've retrofitted with a Sublight Streamdrive engine. Ignus is smoke-testing the Streamdrive now.
Sparck, me boy! Your engine sure is impressive, but I can't seem to get her to spool up to maximum warp.
Have you tried increasing the aperture of the fission intake?
I'm giving her all she's got. I just can't do it. I need more power!
Intriguing. It will take some time for me to properly diagnose the issue.
I trust you'll figure it out, Sparck. Now, if that's all, I've another mission-related task I need to tend to.
Yes, of course. Thank you for your assistance, Ignus. Understudy, we should make haste with the tour.
These stately doors lead to the surprisingly spacious living quarters.
Say what you will about the Cabal, the en suite lavatories are far more comfortable than those here in the Arcanum. Moving on...
This is the Emergency Escape Pod Bay. The Pods are superfluous to our mission, but removing them all would require too much effort.
Here we find the heart of my Intra-Aethyrial Navigational Guidance System: the Lux Capacitor.
It uses quantum photon superpositioning to breach nanospace, allowing the Ark to travel through the stormy Aethyr subatomically.
Its design came to me after I slipped and hit my head in the aforementioned cramped Arcanum lavatory. Shall we continue to the Bridge?
Our tour comes to its conclusion here on the Bridge.
There under the Main Viewer is the Cyclolabe. It will help us plot courses through the Aethyr. A storm compass, as it were.
And we will end the tour with the one detail technology cannot update: the Captain's chair. Rather, the person in it.
Without a Sky Captain experienced in Aethyrial travel, the chair and this mission are utterly futile.
Fortunately, the Scholars have this issue mostly figured out. It would be prudent for you to check on that. I really should get back to work.
'Bout time! We should've told Sparck to skip the lavatory tour. Listen up, we need to discuss the recruitment of the Sky Captain.
There we are! The homemade World Door is secured and ready for transport. You sure we shouldn't test it first?
This World Door will serve as the initial Streamportal link in what I hope will eventually become an Empyrean-wide teleportation network.
Ahh... Kinda like how a lead climber does that first free climb to install the guide rope so everyone else can use it to scale the mountain.
I suppose so, yes.
Just gotta get that first anchor point down, right- Oh, hey there, Understudy. 'Scuse me, I need to check the status of the hull.
Perhaps you recall seeing it referenced when you read <ITALICS>The History of the Great Schism</ITALICS>?
Those who would become the Cabal built it as a lifeboat to usher them through the violent end of the Spiral that they believed inevitable.
After the Schism, the Spiral Ark was forgotten, until a young man with an incorrigible interest in technology found it here collecting dust.
As fate would have it, that young man, named Sparck, hails from Empyrea and has dedicated his life to solving the enigma of Empyrean travel.
And despite my many objections, he has volunteered to accompany you on this mission. He is also my brother. But that is inconsequential.
You and Sparck should become acquainted. Here, give him this Ion Dust he requested, and lend him any further aid he may require.
Sparck said that Ion Dust is crucial for some technical thing in the Spiral Ark that I didn't quite understand. Deliver it to him immediately.
